civil.senne: Ung county (Ung vármegye, Užská župa). Estate of Pavlovce nad Uhom; Vécsey lands.
civil.inacovce: Ung county. Lands of Vécsey, Barkóczy and Szirmay, later Thuránszky and Török.
civil.records: County and estate papers in Latin and Hungarian. Tax censuses 1715, 1720, 1828; urbarial survey; census 1869.

civil.senne: Six districts in the county: Nagyberezna, Nagykapos, Perecseny, Szerednye, Szobránc, Ungvár. Which one Szenna sat in is not yet checked (see PL-H-004).
civil.inacovce: As Senné: the district of Solymos is not yet checked.
civil.records: State civil registration from 1 October 1895, kept beside the church books.

civil.senne: Frontier fixed by the Treaty of Trianon, 4 June 1920. Veľké Kapušany district.
civil.records: Records turn to Slovak. Censuses 1921 and 1930. Land reform files on the Vécsey estate after 1921.

civil.senne: First Vienna Award, 2 November 1938: Uzhhorod returns to Hungary and Ung county is recreated on the Hungarian side. Senné stays in Slovakia.
civil.records: No change of record-keeper for either village.

civil.senne: Little War, 23 to 31 March 1939. Blatná Polianka, Bežovce and Vysoká nad Uhom are taken; the border ends up about 2 km from the village. Senné is counted in the Michalovce district in 1940.
civil.inacovce: Counted in the Michalovce district in 1940. The whole Sobrance district next door goes to Hungary on 4 April 1939.
civil.records: Slovak state records throughout. Neither village has Hungarian-administration records for the war years.

civil.senne: Soviet troops enter on 27 November 1944. Veľké Kapušany district, Prešov region.
civil.records: The eastern part of old Ung county, with Uzhhorod and its archives, passes to the Soviet Union in 1945.

civil.senne: Michalovce district, East Slovak region; now Košice Region.
civil.inacovce: Michalovce district, East Slovak region; now Košice Region.
civil.records: Church registers older than 1895 were gathered into the state archives; civil books follow 100 years after their last entry.

church.covers: Senné, and the Roman Catholics of Iňačovce. In 1734 also Palín, Stretava, Stretavka, Rebrín, Kráška, Jastrabie and Blatná Polianka.

steps.what: A church is thought to have stood here. A church and rectory are recorded in 1599.
Parish rebuilt step by step after the Rákóczi rising. Church built in 1718.
Diocese of Eger. Visited in 1734: 56 Latin-rite adults, about 40 of the Greek rite, 20 Calvinists, 2 Lutherans.
Ung county passes to the new Diocese of Szatmár. Bishop's circulars now come from Szatmár, as in the Duska agent's Folder 1.
The part of the Szatmár diocese left in Czechoslovakia was run separately and later joined to Košice. Dates not yet checked.
Archdiocese of Košice, deanery of Sobrance.

church.covers: Iňačovce. Probably the Greek Catholics of Senné as well (PL-H-001).

steps.what: The Greek Catholics of Iňačovce have their own parish; Rusyn is spoken in it.
Wooden church of the Dormition, shingle roof, one bell.
Eparchy of Mukachevo erected in 1771, with the bishop at Uzhhorod. By 1782 its parishes in Ung county no longer answer to the Latin bishop.
Parish reorganisation papers drawn up for every parish in Ung county. Not yet read for Solymos.
Present brick church built. Register kept from 1811.
A reorganisation leaves Ung county in the Mukachevo eparchy. Its Uzhhorod archdeaconry has eight deaneries.
Parishes left on the Slovak side were placed under the bishop of Prešov. The church was suppressed from 1950 to 1968. Dates not yet checked.
Greek Catholic diocese of Košice.

church.covers: The Reformed of Iňačovce, a daughter congregation.

steps.what: Reformed mother churches near the villages: Stretava, Lúčky, Veľké Zalužice. Iňačovce is not named under any of them in the summary read.
Register for the Iňačovce Reformed begins. It is kept in another parish.
Own school in Iňačovce: 14 pupils, then 41. Part of the Ung Reformed seniorate.
Daughter church built in Iňačovce.

church.covers: The few Lutherans of Iňačovce; the Jewish families of both villages.

steps.what: Lutherans of Iňačovce belonged to the Pozdišovce congregation. Its Jewish families came under the rabbinate at Senné.
Register of Jews: 20 people in Senné, 13 in Iňačovce. Four families were deported from Senné.
